_about: Why each class and relation exists, the alternatives considered, and who confirmed it.

Board.question: Which columns are over their limit, which cards are blocked, how often do we finish within the expected time? (KB1, KB2, KB12 and every board question)
Board.why: Every question is asked about one board; the board carries the expectation the team gives people, so the promise sits with the board that makes it.
Board.alternatives: The team as the anchor: rejected, a team can run more than one board, and the questions are about the flow, not the people.
Board.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-11-02 (walked through in the ontology interview)

Column.question: Where does work pile up, did a card move backwards, what must be true to enter a column? (KB1, KB3, KB5, KB9, KB14)
Column.why: A column has an order, a kind, limits and policies of its own, and every move points at one; it is a thing, not a value on the card.
Column.alternatives: A status value on the card: rejected, a status has no order, no limit and no policy. A fixed list of states (to do, doing, done): rejected, every team draws its own columns.
Column.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-11-02 (walked through in the ontology interview)

Card.question: Who is working on what, how long did this card take, which fixed-date cards are at risk? (KB4, KB7, KB11)
Card.why: The unit that flows: it has its own dates, urgency and history, and it is what every move, blocker and replenishment is about.
Card.alternatives: Separate classes for story, task and bug: rejected, no question tells them apart yet; a card type can come in as a value when one does.
Card.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-11-02 (walked through in the ontology interview)

Move.question: What did the board look like on a date, how long did a card take, how many cards did we finish each week? (KB6, KB7, KB10)
Move.why: Its own node because it has a date and must keep its history: a column written on the card says where it is, never how long it has been there or where it went back from.
Move.alternatives: The card's column as an attribute, superseded on every move: rejected, the questions read the history and a question sees only current facts. Times of day: rejected, dates are compared and flow is read per day, so one move per card per day.
Move.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-11-02 (walked through in the ontology interview)

WipLimit.question: Which columns are over their limit, and when and why did a limit change? (KB1, KB8)
WipLimit.why: A limit is a decision: it has a date, a reason and someone who took it, and the reason for the last change is what the next one starts from.
WipLimit.alternatives: A number on the column: rejected, it keeps no date, no reason and no history. A policy with a number: rejected, a limit is counted against and a policy is read.
WipLimit.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-11-02 (walked through in the ontology interview)

Blocker.question: Which cards are blocked, since when, on whom, and what blocks us most often? (KB2, KB15)
Blocker.why: It has its own start and end dates, a reason and whom it waits on; counted over time it shows the dependencies that keep coming back.
Blocker.alternatives: A blocked flag on the card: rejected, a flag keeps no reason, no dates and no history. A Blocked column: rejected, a blocked card stays in its column.
Blocker.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-11-02 (walked through in the ontology interview)

Policy.question: What has to be true before a card moves into or out of a column, and which policies does this board have that another doesn't? (KB5, KB16)
Policy.why: An explicit policy is a statement the team agreed and can change; it governs a column or a board and is compared across boards.
Policy.alternatives: Text on the column: rejected, a column can have several policies, one on entry and one on exit, and a board has policies of its own.
Policy.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-11-02 (walked through in the ontology interview)

Replenishment.question: Which cards were pulled in at the last replenishment meeting, and who decided? (KB13)
Replenishment.why: The meeting is an event with a date and a decision; the cards chosen and who chose them belong to it, not to each card.
Replenishment.alternatives: A pulled-in date on each card: rejected, it loses who decided and which cards were chosen together.
Replenishment.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-11-02 (walked through in the ontology interview)

Person.question: Who is working on what, who decided a limit or a replenishment, who is a card waiting on? (KB4, KB8, KB13, KB2)
Person.why: In kanban individuals pull the work, and holding more than one card is a question about a person; decisions on a board are taken by named people.
Person.alternatives: Roles, the usual owner because roles outlive people: rejected here, no question is about a role and every one about holding or deciding is about a person.
Person.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-11-02 (walked through in the ontology interview)

Team.question: What or whom are cards waiting on, and how do another team's board's policies differ? (KB15, KB16)
Team.why: Work often waits on another team rather than a person, and boards are compared team to team.
Team.alternatives: Waiting on a person in that team: rejected, the team is what the blocker names and what has to change.
Team.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-11-02 (walked through in the ontology interview)

column_of.question: Which columns does this board have? (every board question)
column_of.why: Every board question walks from the board to its columns.
column_of.alternatives: Columns shared between boards: rejected, each board draws its own.
column_of.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-11-02 (walked through in the ontology interview)

owned_by.question: Which team's board is the other one? (KB16)
owned_by.why: Comparing boards is comparing teams' ways of working.
owned_by.alternatives: The team as a value on the board: rejected, a team is also what a card waits on.
owned_by.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-11-02 (walked through in the ontology interview)

worked_by.question: Who is working on what, and who holds more than one card? (KB4)
worked_by.why: The one edge from the work to the people doing it.
worked_by.alternatives: The person on each move: rejected, the question is who holds the card now.
worked_by.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-11-02 (walked through in the ontology interview)

move_of.question: Where is a card now, and where has it been? (KB1-KB4, KB6, KB7, KB9-KB12, KB14, KB15)
move_of.why: Ties each move to the card it moves; the latest one is where the card is.
move_of.alternatives: Moves listed on the card: rejected, a move has its own date and columns.
move_of.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-11-02 (walked through in the ontology interview)

into.question: Where did a card go, and when? (KB1-KB4, KB6, KB7, KB9-KB12, KB14, KB15)
into.why: The column a move ends in: where the card is from that day.
into.alternatives: Only the target column on the card: rejected, see Move.
into.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-11-02 (walked through in the ontology interview)

out_of.question: Did a card move backwards? (KB9)
out_of.why: Backwards is a move into a column to the left of the one it came out of; the column it left has to be recorded to see it.
out_of.alternatives: Reading the previous move: rejected, the question language finds the previous move only with a second comparison, and a card's first move has none.
out_of.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-11-02 (walked through in the ontology interview)

limits.question: Which columns are over their limit, and how has a limit changed? (KB1, KB8)
limits.why: Ties each limit to the column it limits.
limits.alternatives: Limits on the board: rejected, kanban limits are per column.
limits.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-11-02 (walked through in the ontology interview)

decided_by.question: Who changed a limit, who chose what to pull in? (KB8, KB13)
decided_by.why: Both decisions are taken by named people and asked about by name.
decided_by.alternatives: A separate relation per decision: rejected, one relation means the same thing in both.
decided_by.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-11-02 (walked through in the ontology interview)

blocks.question: Which cards are blocked? (KB2, KB11, KB15)
blocks.why: Ties each blocker to the card it stops, so a blocked card is found from the card and the blocker's dates and reason travel with it.
blocks.alternatives: A blocked flag on the card: rejected, see Blocker.
blocks.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-11-02 (walked through in the ontology interview)

waits_on.question: What or whom is a blocked card waiting on? (KB2, KB15)
waits_on.why: The person, team or card to chase; counted over time, what keeps blocking the board.
waits_on.alternatives: The reason text alone: rejected, a reason in words cannot be grouped by whom it waits on.
waits_on.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-11-02 (walked through in the ontology interview)

applies_to.question: What must be true before a card moves into or out of a column? (KB5)
applies_to.why: A policy governs a column or the whole board.
applies_to.alternatives: Policies on columns only: rejected, some policies hold for the whole board.
applies_to.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-11-02 (walked through in the ontology interview)

policy_of.question: Which policies does this board have that another doesn't? (KB16)
policy_of.why: Gathers every policy that holds on a board, its own and its columns', so two boards can be compared; derived by two rules, never written by hand.
policy_of.alternatives: Asking the question twice, once for the board and once for its columns: rejected, the comparison needs both in one answer.
policy_of.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-11-02 (walked through in the ontology interview)

replenishes.question: What was pulled in at the last replenishment for this board? (KB13)
replenishes.why: Ties a meeting to the board whose work it chose.
replenishes.alternatives: Meetings across boards: rejected, no question asks about one yet.
replenishes.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-11-02 (walked through in the ontology interview)

pulled_in.question: Which cards were pulled in at the last replenishment? (KB13)
pulled_in.why: The cards the meeting chose together, so the next replenishment can look back at what was chosen and what came of it.
pulled_in.alternatives: A pulled-in date on each card: rejected, see Replenishment.
pulled_in.validated_by: Chiheb Dkhil, 2026-11-02 (walked through in the ontology interview)
